text.title: Cognitive Walkthrough: Process Decision Tree
text.summary: Routes on session readiness rather than on the inspection itself: whether all four prerequisites exist before scheduling, who is in the room and how long the task runs, and how the session record is kept — to a full session, a panel or variant correction, or a cancellation.

decision-tree.root-question: As the session is being scheduled, which of the four prerequisites are actually in hand — user description with prior knowledge, one specific task, the correct action sequence, and an interface representation per state?

branch.when: any one of the four is missing or would be filled in from memory during the session

conclusion.verdict: cancel and reschedule once the missing input exists; a session run in reduced form produces disagreements about which interface was inspected, read afterwards as findings about the interface

branch.when: the question the session is meant to answer is task time, error rate or satisfaction for trained users rather than first-use learnability

conclusion.verdict: skip: no walkthrough panel measures performance — route to moderated usability testing and keep the walkthrough for the learnability question

branch.when: all four prerequisites are assembled and the session is being staffed and scoped
branch.question: Who will sit in the room, and how many atomic steps does the task actually run to?

branch.when: one evaluator, or everyone available worked on the design under test

conclusion.verdict: record the output as an inspection draft, not a walkthrough result, until at least one evaluator who did not work on the design joins — a designer's yes on Q2 and Q3 carries no information

branch.when: more than four people are invited

conclusion.verdict: cut the panel to 2-4 named evaluators; above four, step-by-step discussion outruns the session and the later steps get waved through

branch.when: the task runs well past roughly 20 atomic steps, or past a 60-90 minute budget at four questions per step

conclusion.verdict: declare the variant up front: split at sub-goal boundaries into separate sessions, or switch to the streamlined two-question form and record which was used — a form whose final third is uniformly yes is the tell for the alternative

branch.when: 2-4 named evaluators with at least one outside the design, and the task fits the four-question form inside one session

conclusion.verdict: apply the full process: record ground rules, run the four-question form per step, keep each evaluator's answers, then synthesise

branch.when: the session is running or has just finished and the open question is how the record is kept
branch.question: What is happening to the answers and the issue list?

branch.when: the room keeps stopping to defend the design or to design fixes mid-step

conclusion.verdict: park every proposed fix and enforce the ground rule; one design argument eats the budget for a dozen steps and the group compensates by answering the rest yes

branch.when: per-step answers are being collapsed into a single group verdict, or the most senior person's answer settles disagreements

conclusion.verdict: retain each evaluator's own Q1-Q4 answers and record the split in `evaluator_consensus` — a divided answer is the strongest available signal that the step is genuinely ambiguous

branch.when: issues are being written without the step index and without which of Q1-Q4 failed

conclusion.verdict: tag every issue before it enters `prioritized_findings`; the failed question fixes the routing — Q1 entry point, Q2 visibility, Q3 wording, Q4 feedback

branch.when: findings are being ordered by how severe they feel, with an unfixed blocker sitting at an early step

conclusion.verdict: order by earliest blocking step index, state that later findings are conditional on it, and re-walk the tail after the early fix rather than shipping tail fixes as verified
